statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. U.S. stock futures show a modest post-FOMC recovery in Asian trading, while firm front-end yields and a stronger dollar keep rates stress high; direct live NQ retracement structure remains unverified.
recommendation: Tail remains below WATCH; the next concentrated risk window is the 12:30 UTC U.S. data cluster through the early cash-open sequence.
headline: Tail remains low as futures recover modestly while post-FOMC rates stress stays extreme
body: The Fed raised its target range to 3.75%-4.00%. Asian shares are modestly firmer and U.S. stock futures are recovering slightly, while short-term Treasury yields and the dollar remain elevated. Oil is extending losses and fresh latest-session megacap and semiconductor breadth is mixed-positive. Without verified persistent NQ extension or failed retracements, Tail remains low while rates/event Stress stays extreme.

lookbackSummary: Tail stayed low before FOMC, rose to WATCH and briefly reached 25% elevated during repricing, then eased through the evening and returned to low overnight as two-way price discovery reasserted itself.
outlookSummary: Tail is low overnight if price discovery remains two-way, then rises conditionally to WATCH around the 12:30 UTC U.S. data cluster and cash-open sequence; no future release result or directional path is assumed.

forecast.analysis: If early Globex remains two-way with ordinary pullbacks, Tail should stay low; renewed yield-led repeated extension would be the main contrary signal.
If Asian-session trading remains balanced rather than one-way, Tail should remain low while the post-FOMC rates repricing continues to support high Stress.
If the overnight range remains orderly with meaningful retracements, the prior two-way post-FOMC reference path should continue to weigh against a pathological trend.
If early-European liquidity develops without repeated NQ extension, Tail should remain low; persistent yield pressure would mainly keep Stress elevated.
If the Europe handoff remains balanced, Tail should stay low; alignment of higher yields with broad technology weakness would be the key escalation condition.
If European trading remains two-way and pullbacks continue to hold, Tail should remain low despite residual post-FOMC uncertainty.
If pre-U.S. trading remains balanced, Tail should stay low; an abnormal directional gap with failed retracements would be the main reason to reassess.
If futures retain ordinary retracements into the U.S. morning, Tail should remain low while attention shifts toward the scheduled 12:30 UTC data cluster.

As the 12:30 UTC releases approach, Stress rises on event uncertainty and Tail reaches WATCH conditionally; escalation above WATCH would require pre-release price action to become persistently one-way.

The 12:30 UTC U.S. release cluster is a conditional whipsaw checkpoint. Tail reaches WATCH on event-path uncertainty, but a block would require observed persistent extension or failed retracements after the data.
The U.S. cash open follows the 12:30 UTC data cluster. WATCH remains conditional on opening-auction behavior; ordinary two-way discovery would argue against escalation above this band.

If the scheduled 14:00 UTC Pending Home Sales release and early post-open phase remain two-way, Tail should ease below WATCH; persistent extension after failed retracements would be the contrary path.
If post-open price discovery becomes two-way after the scheduled releases, Tail should fall back below WATCH even while rates-related Stress remains high.
If the afternoon develops with ordinary pullbacks and no repeated extension, Tail should remain low as the data-driven repricing window recedes.
If cross-asset signals remain mixed rather than directionally aligned, Tail should remain low; a renewed yield-and-tech one-way move would be the main invalidation.
If the U.S. afternoon remains two-way, Tail should remain low while Stress continues to decay from the event cluster.
If late-session trading stays orderly without failed retracements, Tail should remain low despite the still-elevated rates backdrop.
If power-hour conditions remain balanced rather than directional, Tail should remain low; persistent closing-auction extension would be the escalation checkpoint.
If the cash close completes without a one-way second leg, Tail should remain low and Stress should continue to normalize.
If early post-close trading remains stable, Tail should stay low as immediate U.S. event risk fades.
If overnight liquidity remains orderly, Tail should remain low; the next meaningful scheduled U.S. catalysts are Friday's industrial-production and Fed-speaker window.
If the early Friday Globex session remains two-way, Tail should remain low while attention gradually shifts toward industrial production and Fed communication.
If Asian-session conditions remain balanced into Friday, Tail should stay low; later U.S. industrial production and Fed communication remain conditional checkpoints rather than current Tail evidence.
